 Owing to the repetitive combinatorial formulas of the *Yamaka*, the text shares its largest volumes of text reuse with neighboring chapters of the *Anusayayamaka*, particularly the *Pariññāvāra* (Ya 7.2.4; 8,650 matches), the *Pajahanavāra* (Ya 7.2.3; 7,124 matches), the *Anusayavāra* (Ya 7.2.1; 3,260 matches), and the *Pahīnavāra* (Ya 7.2.5; 2,676 matches), as well as the *Uppattiṭṭhānavāra* (Ya 7.1) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares passages with the Abhidhamma commentary (*Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*) and its subcommentaries (*Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā*, *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā*), the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, the *Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga* (Vb 17), the *Ñāṇavibhaṅga* (Vb 16), the *Ñāṇakathā* of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1), and the *Sattakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 7) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns segments with Sanskrit and Tibetan treatises analyzing defilements (*anuśaya*), including Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* and its commentaries, Vimalamitra's *Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti* and *Abhidharmadīpakārikā*, and the *Abhidharmasamuccaya* [DharmaNexus].
